claim: Analogical mapping is chosen by three soft pressures at once (structure/isomorphism, semantic similarity, purpose/pragmatic centrality), not by a hard structural rule. A constraint-satisfaction network (ACME) settles on one best mapping, usually within 100 cycles (max 220 in reported runs).
agent_test: Make the agent score each candidate mapping on three separate lines (relation fit, feature fit, goal fit) before choosing; compare with single-score choice at equal tokens on a mapping benchmark.

claim: Goal changes which mapping is chosen when structure is ambiguous. Spellman and Holyoak 1996 Exp1: trade goal sent Anthar to Grandus 54% vs Minutus 19%; membership goal reversed it, 21% vs 58% (chi2(1,N=53)=11.78).
agent_test: Run the same ambiguous mapping task with two stated goals; check the agent's mapping flips as humans do and that stating the goal first helps.

claim: Goal acts as attenuation, not a hard filter: goal-irrelevant relations still leak into the mapping (65% followed the incidental inheritance relation in Exp3; 50% many-to-one in the Exp2 control) while plot extension used only the goal-relevant theme (97%).
agent_test: Check whether an agent told to ignore irrelevant structure still lets it change its mapping; measure leakage rate.

claim: Goals matter only for elements that are structurally ambiguous. Unambiguous elements stay stable (about 90% in all five goal conditions in Exp2).
agent_test: Use the goal as a tie-breaker only when top mappings are close; test against always-apply-goal at equal tokens.

claim: Mapping can be bistable: the same situation supports two internally consistent mappings (Gulf War: US=US-WW2 or US=Britain), and a slightly biased summary can steer which one people pick. Gap search: Spellman and Holyoak 1992 Exp1 Table 1 (N=42): Bush=FDR with US=US-WW2 21, FDR with Britain 2, Churchill with US-WW2 6, Churchill with Britain 13 (81% consistent, chi2=16.16); Exp2 N=50 88% consistent, and slanted histories pushing crossed pairs failed (86% still consistent). Same lab only.
agent_test: Ask the agent to generate both consistent mappings explicitly instead of one; measure whether it flags the ambiguity.

claim: Surface similarity and structure both shape spontaneous transfer: Holyoak and Koh convergence problem gave 69/38/33/13% spontaneous solutions across the four surface-by-structure versions. ARCS reproduces the order for retrieval; retrieval and mapping dissociate (Keane: 88% vs 12% retrieval, solving about 86% either way once cued).
agent_test: Test agent retrieval of past solutions with surface-similar vs structure-similar distractors; then test solving once the source is cued.

claim: Under high relational load, people weight object similarity about as much as relational structure (mappings O .33, R .30, SO .32, U .06; N=48). SME, which ranks structure first, scored the relational inference 6.21 vs 1.01 for the object inference and did not reproduce the human mixture; LISA with soft constraints did (24% / 18% / 48%). Gap search: Webb 2023 digit matrices: accuracy fell with the number of unique rules (humans OR=0.61, GPT-3 OR=0.25), so LLMs are more load-sensitive; load shift toward object similarity not tested in LLMs.
agent_test: Vary relational load and measure when the agent over-trusts surface match. Contested with structure-first work (Gentner, Markman) done at lower load.

claim: ACME is parameter-robust but has failure modes: excitation above .12 is unstable, high inhibition can lock in an early wrong mapping, and in the unsystematic cross-mapped Jealous Animals version it fails to find the right mapping.
agent_test: Keep the top two mappings alive for some steps; compare with greedy first-mapping at equal tokens.

claim: Systematicity (structure) matters mainly when similarity is misleading (cross-mapped stories); when similarity agrees with structure, structure adds little to mapping difficulty in ACME.
agent_test: Build cross-mapped items (similar objects in wrong roles) and measure how often the agent falls for the surface match.

claim: Pragmatic support speeds non-isomorphic mappings: Socrates-midwife settled in 34 (isomorphic), 105 (non-isomorphic) and 83 (non-isomorphic with pragmatic support) cycles.
agent_test: Compare mapping with and without a stated purpose on messy non-isomorphic analogies.

claim: Base GPT-3 matched or beat students on text matrix reasoning (digit matrices OR 1.88 generative, 6.27 multiple choice; N=40), letter strings and verbal analogies, but was worse on story analogies (OR 0.37, N=54), especially far ones; GPT-4 was far better.
agent_test: Report far vs near story analogy accuracy for our base model as a baseline before adding any scaffold.

claim: The zero-shot letter-string result does not generalise cleanly. With counterfactual alphabets GPT-3/3.5/4 drop while humans stay high (human .753 overall); Webb et al. reply that GPT-4 with code execution reaches human level, locating the failure in position counting. Gap search: Webb 2024 reply reports N=99/97 humans, GPT-4+code vs humans P=0.496, plain GPT-4 worse P=8.9e-13; controls with a new alphabet (P=0.52) and an older engine (P=0.12); 46% (23/50) of GPT-4+code errors were valid alternative rules. Counting is the main cause; still same-lab evidence.
agent_test: Test counterfactual-alphabet items with and without code execution; see at equal tokens whether a calculation tool closes the gap.

claim: LLMs are weaker when the correct story is far and a distractor is surface-similar. ARN (1,096 triples): far analogies 39.6% (below the 50% chance) vs humans 94.1%; near 75.0% vs 97.9%; far analogy vs near distractor 33.9%. StoryAnalogy multiple choice: ChatGPT about 30% vs humans 85.7% (chance 25%). Gap search: on the 18 Gentner stories with order balanced, 2024 models reach about .82-.85 conventional (gpt-4o, Llama-3.1-70B) vs humans .847 and GPT-3 .75, so the far-analogy gap shrinks on small story sets; ARN far-distractor items untested on reasoning models.
agent_test: Run ARN-style far-vs-near-distractor items with and without a forced relational-description step.

claim: GPT-4 story-analogy accuracy has an answer-order bias (correct first 0.89 vs second 0.61 in Webb's data; 1.0 vs 0.72 in Lewis and Mitchell's run) that humans lack (0.78 both). Paraphrase drops GPT-4 0.86 to 0.72 and humans 0.78 to 0.70. Gap search: Inani et al. 2025 balanced order 50/50 over 100 runs per item, so order was controlled, not measured; no new order-bias estimate for 2025 models.
agent_test: Randomise option order and run both orders; count disagreement as unreliability.

claim: LLM letter-string errors differ in kind from human errors. Humans: 38.59% alternate-rule errors; GPT-4 22.00%; GPT-3 5.81%. Incorrect-rule errors: humans 14.67%, GPT-4 32.67%, GPT-3 30.97%.
agent_test: Classify our agent's analogy errors into alternate-rule vs wrong-rule to see whether it explores valid alternatives.

claim: LLM analogy skill depends on domain familiarity; humans' does not. Letter-string accuracy Latin/Greek/Symbol: adults .88/.91/.89, children .62/.66/.67, GPT-4o .85/.63/.48, Claude-3.5 .68/.62/.46, Llama-3.1 405B .79/.74/.27, Gemma-2 27B .60/.39/.14.
agent_test: Re-encode unfamiliar-domain items into abstract roles before mapping; compare to raw prompting at equal tokens.

claim: Some model success comes from association with the target term, not relation: controlling for association lowered Dutch LLM scores by 1-2 age years.
agent_test: Include association-controlled distractors in mapping tests.

claim: Presentation order and irrelevant semantic content disturb LLM mapping more than human mapping in some conditions; best models match or beat humans in others (Musker et al. 2025). Gap search (Musker 2025 detail): with random left-hand words humans drop about .15, Claude 3 about .5, GPT-4 .6 and .4; in the 2x-infinity follow-up Claude 3 and humans about .7 vs GPT-4 and Llama-405B about .35; GPT-4 .2-.3 on Numeric conditions.
agent_test: Shuffle order and add a semantic distractor; count answer changes.

claim: Forced abstraction before mapping helps: raw embedding-based structural mapping is below chance on ARN MCQ (Qwen 0.17 vs chance 0.25), but LLM abstraction then code-based one-to-one mapping reaches 0.46 vs 0.41 best LLM-only (Llama 0.45 vs 0.28).
agent_test: Replicate: two-stage (abstract roles, then constraint-checked mapping) vs single-prompt at equal tokens.

claim: Structured analogy steps can raise idea diversity: object/relation extraction plus function-based cross-domain analogy raised solution Vendi 90-173% and novel solutions above 50% vs as low as 1.6% (Shen et al. 2026). Random cross-domain sources help humans but not most LLMs (Liu et al. 2026).
agent_test: Compare structured-analogy generation to random-source prompting on diversity and correctness at equal tokens.

claim: Self-generated exemplars (analogical prompting) give small gains over CoT: GSM8K GPT-3.5 75.0 (0-shot), 75.8 (0-shot CoT), 76.7 (5-shot CoT), 77.8 (self-generated); average +4% across tasks. This is related work, not a test of mapping choice.
agent_test: Test self-recalled problem plus an explicit mapping step vs recall without mapping.

claim: Purpose (pragmatic) constraint is the least handled constraint in NLP and LLM analogy work; proposals exist (neuro-symbolic, goal-weighted attention) but no measured LLM replication of goal-driven mapping reversal was found. Gap search: a 2025 survey (Petersen et al.) again lists goal-driven mapping as open; still no measured LLM replication.
agent_test: Run the Spellman and Holyoak Anthar task on our agent with trade vs membership goals; first LLM replication.

claim: Successor model PAM (probabilistic analogical mapping) reproduces human mapping and the goal effect: keyword analogies 85% vs adult humans 88%; Category triplets .83 vs .74 humans and Part-Object-Location .89 vs .79 (N=1,329); goal-focus correlation .96 over 10 conditions.
agent_test: Use attention-weighted relation similarity as the scoring rule for candidate mappings.

claim: Relational priming and relation use are strategic, not automatic: priming appeared only when people were told to note and use the relation (25 ms, F(1,23)=36.54).
agent_test: Check whether an explicit instruction to list relations is needed to get relational mapping in the agent.

claim: Original ACME and ARCS fits to human data are ordinal only; the ARCS fit broke 75% of the time when 25% of units were deleted.
agent_test: Treat the model as qualitative guidance, not calibrated weights.

claim: Spellman and Holyoak 1992 Exp3 (science fiction, N=59 retained, 46 mapped): one-to-many mappings occurred in 41% of the crossed condition vs 0% of the consistent condition (chi2(1,N=46)=9.75). One-to-one is a strong but soft preference.
agent_test: Allow the agent to output a flagged one-to-many mapping when two source roles both fit; check it does so only when forced.

claim: Irrelevant structure leaks into LLM mappings more than into human ones: with random left-hand items GPT-4 and Claude 3 lose about .4-.6 match while humans lose about .15; frontier models differ (Claude 3 human-level on the widened task, GPT-4 and Llama-405B about .35 vs .7).
agent_test: Insert irrelevant but similar-looking items in mapping tasks; compare with and without an explicit 'drop what is irrelevant to the goal' step.

claim: A 2-step prompt in which the model writes hints about the causal structure before choosing raised accuracy for all four tested models on the 18 Gentner story analogies (best about .915 for Llama-3.1-70B vs .8538 conventional), but made item difficulty less like humans (item correlation fell for 3 of 4 models).
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of hint-then-choose vs direct choice on fresh far-analogy items.

claim: Application of a known relation to a new entity, not only extraction of the relation, is a failure point in open LLMs: patching representations fixed +49.8% to +61.9% of errors in three 7-14B models, and story success tracks source-target structural alignment.
schema_part: S4 split: name relation, then apply
agent_test: Two-step mapping prompt (state relation; apply to target entity) vs one step on proportional analogies.

claim: No independent lab has replicated the Spellman and Holyoak 1996 goal-reversal; the one independent test found (Colhoun and Gentner 2009) targets causal-inference evaluation in the same school and gives a competing post-mapping explanation, not a failed replication.
agent_test: Run our own replication with N over 200 on the base model as well as on people if possible.
